messages.content: I need to settle the New Orleans hotel now. Compare the Cambria for all four nights with the less expensive room we saw on the streetcar line. I need the real totals, not just the nightly rates.

I have current quotes for Sunday, January 11 through Thursday, January 15, one room for one adult. Cambria Hotel New Orleans Downtown is $169 per night for four nights, or $676 in room charges. Taxes add $109.85, bringing the complete stay to $785.85. There is no destination fee. The rate requires full payment on January 7 and becomes nonrefundable when charged.

Maison Saint Charles is $142 per night, or $568 for four nights. Its mandatory destination fee is $29 per night, adding $116. Taxes on the room and fee total $111.15, so the complete stay is $795.15. That rate can be canceled without charge until 6:00 p.m. on January 10; payment is collected at check-in.
So the hotel with the lower room rate is actually $9.30 more for the stay?
Correct. Cambria is $785.85 in total, while Maison Saint Charles is $795.15. Once the four nightly destination fees and taxes are included, Cambria costs $9.30 less overall.
Now compare the morning trip to the Contemporary Arts Center. I have to be at 900 Camp by 8:00 Monday, and I do not want an optimistic estimate.

From Cambria, the walk is about 0.4 mile and typically takes 7 to 9 minutes. Allowing time for the main intersections and entry to the building, leaving the hotel at 7:40 a.m. should put you inside by roughly 7:52.

From Maison Saint Charles, the practical trip is about 18 to 25 minutes: a short walk to the St. Charles streetcar stop, roughly 8 to 12 minutes aboard if service is on schedule, then another walk to 900 Camp. Morning waits can vary, so I would leave by 7:20 a.m. to protect the 8:00 arrival.
What about Tuesday and Wednesday? Are there any service changes that make the streetcar option worse?

No scheduled service suspension appears for those mornings, but normal headways and traffic still make the trip variable. A reasonable door-to-door allowance is 25 to 30 minutes each morning from Maison Saint Charles, compared with about 10 to 15 minutes from the Cambria when walking and allowing time to enter the museum.

The Thursday handling matters too. I check out before the 9:00 inspection, finish around noon, and need the exhibition case before going to the airport. Verify both hotels will keep it after checkout, not just an ordinary suitcase.
I need the approximate case dimensions to verify that with the hotels. Do you have them?
It is a hard-sided case, about 44 by 28 by 12 inches, around 46 pounds. There will also be my roller bag.

I checked the stated luggage policies against those details. Both hotels confirmed they can hold the roller bag and one hard-sided exhibition case of that size after Thursday checkout. Storage is at the staffed bell desk, not in the guest room, and neither hotel charges a luggage-storage fee for a departing guest.
Can I leave the case early Thursday, and how late can I retrieve it? I expect to pick it up around 1:00 or 1:15.

Yes. Cambria will accept both items when you check out Thursday morning and hold them until 8:00 p.m. Maison Saint Charles will hold them until 6:00 p.m. Your planned 1:00 to 1:15 p.m. retrieval is comfortably within either window. Both require the claim ticket and photo identification for release.
Does Cambria have someone at the desk early enough for me to check out around 8:15 Thursday?

Yes. Cambria's front desk is staffed around the clock, and bell assistance begins at 7:00 a.m. They can complete checkout and tag both pieces at 8:15 a.m. The hotel also noted that the larger case may remain behind the bell desk rather than in the smaller locked luggage room, but it stays in a staff-controlled area.
That works. Before booking, spell out the payment risk on the Cambria rate. January 7 is several days before I arrive.

The full $785.85 will be charged to the card on January 7. You can cancel without penalty before 11:59 p.m. Central time on January 6. Starting January 7, the entire amount is nonrefundable, including for a shortened stay or no-show. No additional mandatory hotel fee is due at check-in, though the hotel may place a temporary $75 incidental hold.
And the other hotel's cancellation advantage is real even though it costs a little more?

Yes. Maison Saint Charles remains cancelable until 6:00 p.m. Central time on January 10, and its $795.15 stay total is due at check-in. It gives you three additional days before the financial commitment, at a total cost $9.30 higher than Cambria and with the longer, less predictable morning trip.

The inspection is confirmed, and the flights are already fixed, so I am comfortable committing. Reserve the Cambria for January 11 through January 15. One room, one adult, and use the work card already attached to this trip.

Before I submit it: this is the $785.85 advance-purchase rate, charged in full on January 7 and nonrefundable from that date. Should I also add a note about Thursday storage for the 44-by-28-by-12-inch exhibition case and roller bag?
Yes, add that note, including an expected pickup by 1:15 p.m. Then book it.

Cambria Hotel New Orleans Downtown is reserved for one adult from Sunday, January 11 through Thursday, January 15, four nights. The complete total is $785.85 including taxes, with no destination fee. The work card on file will be charged in full on January 7; cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. Central time January 6, after which the stay is nonrefundable. A $75 incidental hold may be placed at check-in.

The reservation notes Thursday morning storage for one 44-by-28-by-12-inch hard-sided exhibition case and one roller bag, with pickup expected by 1:15 p.m. The front desk and bell team confirmed they can accommodate both items after checkout at no charge. Confirmation: CNO-418672.
